ana: Follow-up to RFC: adaptive-risk weighting for canaries. idea: let controller adjust weightings of RiskVector dimensions during a rollout instead of binary flips.

phil: can you sketch the glue? how would router act on a changing weight?

ana: router sends RiskVector (tiny) and controller returns back a per-route WeightSet and an action: {allow, degrade, fallback}. router applies score = dot(RiskVector, WeightSet) locally and compares to local_threshold to decide immediate degrade. controller decisions drive traffic pct over time.

robin: advantages: we get smoother transitions and fewer abrupt fallbacks. also controller can bias against dimensions that cause false-positives (e.g., attachments).

kristy: ops: need safety: controller can be in passive mode for private deployments. also require signed WeightSet and short TTL so router rejects stale config.

ana: proto sketch in words: WeightSet = {v_latency, v_cost, v_quality, schema_version, ttl_secs, signature}. router validates signature, computes score, applies local hysteresis.

phil: testing idea: run dual-controller sim with historical RiskVectors and let proposed weights be evaluated for false-fallback rate. we should enforce max_weight_change_per_min to prevent wild swings.

robin: add a guardrail: controllers can only change weights by +/-10% per minute, and any weight change that increases fallback rate > X% triggers immediate rollback.

kristy: telemetry: emit weight_change events and correlate with false-fallback SLO. dashboards for per-route fallback-rate, detection-latency, and weight-change history.

deploy-bot: rollout policy updated for svc=text-gen-canary (deploy-6789) :rocket:

ana: next steps: I'll draft minimal proto and safety appendix. @phil will run the sim, @robin will update router client to validate signed weights, @kristy will add dashboards.

phil: noted, sim infra slot booked.

robin: will add signature validation and TTL checks. timeline: PR in 2 weeks.

kristy: will add dashboards and SLOs; will also draft emergency-rollback playbook.

ana: thanks team. will post RFC patch and a small diagram.
